title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
prompt:
A path in a binary tree is any sequence of nodes where each pair of adjacent nodes is connected by an edge, and no node appears more than once. A path does not need to pass through the root, and it does not need to be a root-to-leaf path.

Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the maximum possible sum of node values along any path in the tree.

The tree is given as a level-order array where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization). Your function receives this array directly; the starter code includes a helper that builds the tree from it, so you only need to compute the maximum path sum.

examples.explanation: The path 15 -> 20 -> 7 has sum 15 + 20 + 7 = 42, ignoring the negative root.
A single-node tree must use that node as the whole path, even though its value is negative — a path always has at least one node.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [1, 3 * 10^4]
hints: For each node, think about the best downward path that starts at that node and goes into at most one child — this is what a parent can use to extend a path through itself.
At each node, the best 'path through this node' can use both children (as a peak), but that combined value can't be passed up to the parent since a path can't branch.

Do a post-order traversal. At each node, compute the max single-branch gain from each child (clamped at 0 to ignore negative branches), update a global best using node.val + left_gain + right_gain, but return node.val + max(left_gain, right_gain) to the parent.

solution.approach: Use post-order DFS. For each node, recursively get the maximum gain contributed by a downward path starting at each child, clamping negative gains to 0 (since including a negative branch would only hurt the sum). The best path 'through' the current node as its peak is node.val + left_gain + right_gain; track the global maximum across all nodes. However, a node can only pass one branch up to its parent (since a path can't fork), so it returns node.val + max(left_gain, right_gain).
